resources.string: Nothing here can be reached from the tailnet, the local network or the internet
TailSocks is stopped: this is what opens when it starts.
Incoming connections are blocked: no tailnet device can open one to this device.
Anyone on the internet can reach these.
the tailnet\'s policy is not known yet
the tailnet\'s policy does not allow sharing
no token: every broadcast is refused
Served ports anyone on the internet can open, at this device\'s public name. No tailnet account is needed to connect.

This device as a TailCat server: clients that hold its address reach the ports it hands out, and its exit node if it offers one, from anywhere, through Tailscale\'s relays. Without a list of client keys anyone with the address can.
Paired TailSocks devices manage this one over the tailnet. Every other device of the tailnet gets a refusal, and can try a pairing code only while one is shown here.
Paired owners may do more than the basics: share folders, offer the exit node, advertise routes, read diagnostics.
Paired devices may list this device\'s folders and send or fetch files over the tailnet.
A guest was given an owner\'s rights until the time shown. They end by themselves; turning this off ends them now.
Folders of this device that tailnet devices open, wherever the tailnet\'s policy grants them Taildrive.
Your own devices — and any the tailnet\'s policy lets send files — can send files here while TailSocks runs. It has no switch: only blocking incoming connections stops it.
Ports this device serves to the tailnet: web pages, proxies to services on this device, TCP forwards.
Tailnet devices may send all their internet traffic out through this device, once the tailnet\'s admin approves the offer.
Tailnet devices reach these networks through this device, once the tailnet\'s admin approves the routes.
Traffic the tailnet routes through app connectors goes out through this device\'s internet connection.
Tailnet devices that cannot reach each other directly pass their traffic through a UDP port of this device, where the policy lets them. The port is open on this device\'s real networks.
Proxies open to the local network
The SOCKS5 proxy, the HTTP proxy and the DNS proxy listen on every address: anyone on the same Wi-Fi can use them, and the tailnet too.
Apps send their traffic into the tailnet through it, and out through the exit node. Whoever reaches it uses this device\'s connection; a username and a password keep others out.
The same for apps that speak HTTP. It has no password: whoever reaches it can use it.
Answers name lookups, MagicDNS names included: whoever reaches it can look up the tailnet\'s names.
Tailscale\'s web page for this device: whoever opens it sees the device\'s state and can sign it in.
A WebDAV door to every folder the tailnet shares with this device: whoever reaches it opens those folders as this device. Open to the local network, it always asks for a login.
Ports here that lead to TailCat servers, and TailCat\'s SOCKS5 proxies. They listen on 127.0.0.1.
ByeDPI\'s proxy for the control connection, on a random loopback address that nothing outside this device reaches.

In this mode Tailscale hands every connection to this device\'s tailnet address to the same port on 127.0.0.1. So tailnet devices the access rules allow reach every port that listens there or on every address — other apps\' ports too. Blocking incoming connections closes all of it.

The tailnet address is on a real interface: tailnet devices the access rules allow reach every port that listens on every address — other apps\' ports too. Blocking incoming connections closes all of it.
tailscale0 carries the tailnet below Android\'s VPN: the tailnet reaches this device\'s own network stack, every app that listens on every address included.
Starts Tailscale at boot, before the app: what this list shows opens without TailSocks being opened.
Root shells and apps with root can run %1$s and control this device\'s Tailscale. It is installed in /data/adb/service.d and as a module over /system/bin.
Apps on this device that know the token — Tasker, MacroDroid — can connect and disconnect, and switch exit nodes and accounts.
Assistant apps Android lets in can read the connection, the devices and the accounts; with external automation allowed they can also connect and change settings.
Only apps on this device reach it.
In this mode Tailscale hands connections to this device\'s tailnet address to the same port on 127.0.0.1: that is how the tailnet reaches it.
It listens on every address: the local network reaches it, and so does the tailnet.
It listens on an address of the local network, which reaches it.
It listens on this device\'s tailnet address.
